source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Cable colour non-conformance

requirement_text: Cables in non-TOP SECRET areas are inspectable every five metres or less.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Cable inspectability

requirement_text: Cables in TOP SECRET areas are fully inspectable for their entire length.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Cable inspectability

requirement_text: SECRET cables, when bundled together or run in conduit, are run exclusively in their own individual cable bundle or conduit.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Common cable bundles and conduits

requirement_text: TOP SECRET cables, when bundled together or run in conduit, are run exclusively in their own individual cable bundle or conduit.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Common cable bundles and conduits

requirement_text: Cable bundles or conduits sharing a common cable reticulation system have a dividing partition or visible gap between each cable bundle and conduit.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Common cable reticulation systems

requirement_text: In shared facilities, cables are run in an enclosed cable reticulation system.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Enclosed cable reticulation systems

requirement_text: In shared facilities, conduits or the front covers of ducts, cable trays in floors and ceilings, and associated fittings are clear plastic.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Covers for enclosed cable reticulation systems

requirement_text: In shared facilities, uniquely identifiable SCEC-approved tamper-evident seals are used to seal all removable covers on TOP SECRET cable reticulation systems.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Sealing cable reticulation systems and conduits

requirement_text: In shared facilities, a visible smear of conduit glue is used to seal all plastic conduit joints and TOP SECRET conduits connected by threaded lock nuts.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Sealing cable reticulation systems and conduits

requirement_text: Labels for TOP SECRET conduits are a minimum size of 2.5 cm x 1 cm, attached at five-metre intervals and marked as ‘TS RUN’.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Labelling conduits

requirement_text: Cables from cable trays to wall outlet boxes are run in flexible or plastic conduit.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Cables in walls

requirement_text: In shared facilities, TOP SECRET cables are not run in party walls.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Cables in party walls

requirement_text: Where wall penetrations exit a TOP SECRET area into a lower classified area, TOP SECRET cables are encased in conduit with all gaps between the TOP SECRET conduit and the wall filled with an appropriate sealing compound.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Wall penetrations

requirement_text: SECRET and TOP SECRET wall outlet boxes contain exclusively SECRET or TOP SECRET cables.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Wall outlet boxes

requirement_text: Wall outlet boxes denote the systems, cable identifiers and wall outlet box identifier.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Labelling wall outlet boxes

requirement_text: Wall outlet boxes for individual systems use a consistent colour.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Wall outlet box colours

requirement_text: Non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED wall outlet boxes are coloured neither salmon pink nor red.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Wall outlet box colours

requirement_text: SECRET wall outlet boxes are coloured salmon pink.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Wall outlet box colours

requirement_text: TOP SECRET wall outlet boxes are coloured red.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Wall outlet box colours

requirement_text: Wall outlet box covers are clear plastic.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Wall outlet box covers

requirement_text: If TOP SECRET fibre-optic fly leads exceeding five metres in length are used to connect wall outlet boxes to IT equipment, they are run in a protective and easily inspected pathway that is clearly labelled at the IT equipment end with the wall outlet box’s identifier.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Fly lead installation

requirement_text: Cable reticulation systems leading into cabinets are terminated as close as possible to the cabinet.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Connecting cable reticulation systems to cabinets

requirement_text: In TOP SECRET areas, cable reticulation systems leading into cabinets in server rooms or communications rooms are terminated as close as possible to the cabinet.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Connecting cable reticulation systems to cabinets

requirement_text: In TOP SECRET areas, cable reticulation systems leading into cabinets not in server rooms or communications rooms are terminated at the boundary of the cabinet.

requirement_text: TOP SECRET cables are terminated in an individual TOP SECRET cabinet.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Terminating cables in cabinets

requirement_text: SECRET and TOP SECRET cables are terminated on their own individual patch panels.

Where spatial constraints demand non-TOP SECRET patch panels be installed in the same cabinet as a TOP SECRET patch panel:

source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Cabling infrastructure > Power reticulation

source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Emanation security > Electromagnetic interference/electromagnetic compatibility standards

requirement_text: Emanation security doctrine produced by ASD for the management of emanation security matters is complied with.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Emanation security > Emanation security doctrine

requirement_text: System owners deploying SECRET or TOP SECRET systems within fixed facilities contact ASD for an emanation security risk assessment.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Emanation security > Emanation security risk assessments

requirement_text: System owners deploying SECRET or TOP SECRET systems in mobile platforms, or as a deployable capability, contact ASD for an emanation security risk assessment.
source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Emanation security > Emanation security risk assessments

source_section: Guidelines for communications infrastructure > Emanation security > Emanation security risk assessments

requirement_text: A telephone system usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.
source_section: Guidelines for communications systems > Telephone systems > Telephone system usage policy

requirement_text: Personnel are advised of the permitted sensitivity or classification of information that can be discussed over internal and external telephone systems.
source_section: Guidelines for communications systems > Telephone systems > Personnel awareness

requirement_text: Personnel are advised of security risks posed by non-secure telephone systems in areas where sensitive or classified conversations can occur.
source_section: Guidelines for communications systems > Telephone systems > Personnel awareness

requirement_text: When using cryptographic equipment to permit different levels of conversation for different kinds of connections, telephone systems give a visual indication of what kind of connection has been made.
source_section: Guidelines for communications systems > Telephone systems > Personnel awareness

requirement_text: Telephone systems used for sensitive or classified conversations encrypt all traffic that passes over external systems.
source_section: Guidelines for communications systems > Telephone systems > Protecting conversations

requirement_text: Cordless telephone handsets and headsets are not used for sensitive or classified conversations unless all communications are encrypted using ASD-approved cryptography.
source_section: Guidelines for communications systems > Telephone systems > Cordless telephone systems

source_section: Guidelines for communications systems > Telephone systems > Speakerphones

requirement_text: Off-hook audio protection features are used on telephone systems in areas where background conversations may exceed the sensitivity or classification that the telephone system is authorised for communicating.
source_section: Guidelines for communications systems > Telephone systems > Off-hook audio protection

requirement_text: In SECRET and TOP SECRET areas, push-to-talk handsets or push-to-talk headsets are used to meet any off-hook audio protection requirements.
source_section: Guidelines for communications systems > Telephone systems > Off-hook audio protection

source_section: Guidelines for communications systems > Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony > Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony infrastructure hardening

requirement_text: When video conferencing or IP telephony traffic passes through a gateway containing a firewall or proxy, a video-aware or voice-aware firewall or proxy is used.
source_section: Guidelines for communications systems > Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony > Video-aware and voice-aware firewalls and proxies

requirement_text: Video conferencing and IP telephony calls are established using a secure session initiation protocol.
source_section: Guidelines for communications systems > Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony > Protecting video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony traffic

requirement_text: Video conferencing and IP telephony calls are conducted using a secure real-time transport protocol.
source_section: Guidelines for communications systems > Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony > Protecting video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony traffic

requirement_text: An encrypted and non-replayable two-way authentication scheme is used for call authentication and authorisation.
source_section: Guidelines for communications systems > Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony > Video conferencing unit and Internet Protocol phone authentication

requirement_text: Authentication and authorisation is used for all actions on a video conferencing network, including call setup and changing settings.
source_section: Guidelines for communications systems > Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony > Video conferencing unit and Internet Protocol phone authentication

requirement_text: Authentication and authorisation is used for all actions on an IP telephony network, including registering a new IP phone, changing phone users, changing settings and accessing voicemail.
source_section: Guidelines for communications systems > Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony > Video conferencing unit and Internet Protocol phone authentication

requirement_text:
IP telephony is configured such that:

- IP phones authenticate themselves to the call controller upon registration
- auto-registration is disabled and only authorised devices are allowed to access the network
- unauthorised devices are blocked by default
- all unused and prohibited functionality is disabled.

requirement_text: IP phones used in public areas do not have the ability to access data networks, voicemail and directory services.

requirement_text: Microphones (including headsets and USB handsets) and webcams are not used with non-TOP SECRET workstations in TOP SECRET areas.
source_section: Guidelines for communications systems > Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony > Microphones and webcams

requirement_text: A denial of service response plan for video conferencing and IP telephony services is developed, implemented and maintained.

requirement_text:
A denial of service response plan for video conferencing and IP telephony services contains the following:

- how to identify the source of a denial-of-service attack
- how capabilities can be maintained during a denial-of-service attack
- what actions can be taken to respond to a denial-of-service attack.
source_section: Guidelines for communications systems > Video conferencing and Internet Protocol telephony > Denial of service response plan

requirement_text: An MFD usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

requirement_text: MFDs are not connected to digital telephone systems.
source_section: Guidelines for communications systems > Multifunction devices > Connecting multifunction devices to digital telephone systems

requirement_text: Authentication measures for MFDs are the same strength as those used for workstations on networks they are connected to.
source_section: Guidelines for communications systems > Multifunction devices > Authenticating to multifunction devices

requirement_text: Privately owned mobile devices and desktop computers do not access SECRET and TOP SECRET systems or data.

source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Enterprise mobility > Organisation-owned mobile devices and desktop computers

source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Enterprise mobility > Mobile devices and desktop computers accessing the internet

requirement_text: When accessing an organisation’s network via a VPN connection, split tunnelling is disabled.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Enterprise mobility > Mobile devices and desktop computers accessing the internet

source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device management > Mobile device management policy

requirement_text: Mobile Device Management solutions that have completed a Common Criteria evaluation against the Protection Profile for Mobile Device Management, version 4.0 or later, are used to enforce mobile device management policy.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device management > Mobile device management policy

requirement_text: Mobile devices that access OFFICIAL: Sensitive or PROTECTED systems or data use mobile platforms that have completed a Common Criteria evaluation against the Protection Profile for Mobile Device Fundamentals, version 3.3 or later, and are operated in accordance with the latest version of their associated ASD security configuration guide.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device management > Approved mobile platforms

source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device management > Encrypted storage

requirement_text: Mobile devices encrypt all sensitive or classified data communicated over public network infrastructure using ASD-approved cryptography.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device management > Encrypted communications

requirement_text: Mobile applications encrypt all sensitive or classified data communicated over public network infrastructure using ASD-approved cryptography.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device management > Encrypted communications

source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device management > Maintaining mobile device security

requirement_text: Mobile devices are configured to enforce separation between organisational and personal mobile applications and data.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device management > Maintaining mobile device security

requirement_text: Mobile devices are configured with always on VPN functionality.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device management > Maintaining mobile device security

requirement_text: Mobile devices are configured with remote locate and wipe functionality.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device management > Maintaining mobile device security

requirement_text: Mobile devices are configured with secure password-based lock screens.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device management > Maintaining mobile device security

requirement_text: Mobile devices are configured to prevent data transfers over Universal Serial Bus connections.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device management > Maintaining mobile device security

requirement_text: Mobile devices prevent personnel from installing non-approved applications once provisioned.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device management > Maintaining mobile device security

requirement_text: Mobile devices prevent personnel from disabling or modifying security functionality once provisioned.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device management > Maintaining mobile device security

requirement_text: Security updates are applied to mobile devices as soon as they become available.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device management > Maintaining mobile device security

requirement_text: A mobile device usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Mobile device usage policy

requirement_text: Personnel are advised of the sensitivity or classification permitted for voice and data communications when using mobile devices.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Personnel awareness

requirement_text:
Personnel are advised to take the following precautions when using mobile devices:

- never leave mobile devices or removable media unattended, including by placing them in checked-in luggage or leaving them in hotel safes
- never store credentials with mobile devices that they grant access to, such as in laptop computer bags
- never lend mobile devices or removable media to untrusted people, even if briefly
- never allow untrusted people to connect their mobile devices or removable media to your mobile devices, including for charging
- never connect mobile devices to designated charging stations or wall outlet charging ports
- never use gifted or unauthorised peripherals, chargers or removable media with mobile devices
- never use removable media for data transfers or backups that have not been checked for malicious code beforehand
- avoid reuse of removable media once used with other parties’ systems or mobile devices
- avoid connecting mobile devices to open or untrusted Wi-Fi networks
- consider disabling any communications capabilities of mobile devices when not in use, such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Near Field Communication and ultra-wideband
- consider periodically rebooting mobile devices
- consider using a VPN connection to encrypt all cellular and wireless communications
- consider using encrypted email or messaging apps for all communications.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Personnel awareness

requirement_text: Paging, Multimedia Message Service, Short Message Service and messaging apps are not used to communicate sensitive or classified data.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Using paging, message services and messaging apps

requirement_text: Non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED mobile devices are configured to remain undiscoverable to other Bluetooth devices except during Bluetooth pairing.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Using Bluetooth functionality

requirement_text: Bluetooth pairing for non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED mobile devices is performed using Secure Connections, preferably with Numeric Comparison if supported.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Using Bluetooth functionality

requirement_text: Bluetooth pairing for non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED mobile devices is performed in a manner such that connections are only made between intended Bluetooth devices.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Using Bluetooth functionality

requirement_text: Bluetooth pairings for non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED mobile devices are removed when there is no longer a requirement for their use.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Using Bluetooth functionality

requirement_text: Bluetooth functionality is not enabled on SECRET and TOP SECRET mobile devices.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Using Bluetooth functionality

requirement_text: Mobile devices are not connected to the infotainment systems of connected vehicles.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Connecting mobile devices to connected vehicles

requirement_text: Sensitive or classified data is not viewed on mobile devices within or near connected vehicles.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Using mobile devices within or near connected vehicles

requirement_text: Sensitive or classified phone calls and conversations are not conducted within or near connected vehicles.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Using mobile devices within or near connected vehicles

requirement_text: Sensitive or classified data is not viewed on mobile devices in public locations unless care is taken to reduce the chance of the screen of a mobile device being observed.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Using mobile devices in public spaces

requirement_text: Privacy filters are applied to the screens of SECRET and TOP SECRET mobile devices.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Using mobile devices in public spaces

requirement_text: Sensitive or classified phone calls and conversations are not conducted in public locations unless care is taken to reduce the chance of conversations being overheard.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Using mobile devices in public spaces

requirement_text: Mobile devices are kept under continual direct supervision when being actively used.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Maintaining control of mobile devices

requirement_text: Mobile devices are carried or stored in a secured state when not being actively used.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Maintaining control of mobile devices

requirement_text: If unable to carry or store mobile devices in a secured state, they are physically transferred in a security briefcase or an approved multi-use satchel, pouch or transit bag.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Maintaining control of mobile devices

requirement_text: Mobile device emergency sanitisation processes, and supporting mobile device emergency sanitisation procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Mobile device emergency sanitisation processes and procedures

requirement_text: If a cryptographic zeroise or sanitise function is provided for cryptographic keys on a SECRET or TOP SECRET mobile device, the function is used as part of mobile device emergency sanitisation processes and procedures.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Mobile device emergency sanitisation processes and procedures

requirement_text: Personnel are advised of privacy and security risks when travelling overseas with mobile devices.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Before travelling overseas with mobile devices

requirement_text:
If travelling overseas with mobile devices to high or extreme risk countries, personnel are:

- issued with newly provisioned user accounts, mobile devices and removable media from a pool of dedicated travel devices which are used solely for work-related activities
- advised on how to apply and inspect tamper seals to key areas of mobile devices
- advised to avoid taking any personal mobile devices, especially if rooted or jailbroken.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Before travelling overseas with mobile devices

requirement_text:
Before travelling overseas with mobile devices, personnel take the following actions:

- record all details of the mobile devices being taken, such as product types, serial numbers and International Mobile Equipment Identity numbers
- update all operating systems and applications
- remove all non-essential data, applications and user accounts
- backup all remaining data, applications and settings.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > Before travelling overseas with mobile devices

requirement_text:
Personnel report the potential compromise of mobile devices, removable media or credentials to their organisation as soon as possible, especially if they:

- provide credentials to foreign government officials
- decrypt mobile devices for foreign government officials
- have mobile devices taken out of sight by foreign government officials
- have mobile devices or removable media stolen, including if later returned
- lose mobile devices or removable media, including if later found
- observe unusual behaviour of mobile devices.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > While travelling overseas with mobile devices

requirement_text:
Upon returning from travelling overseas with mobile devices, personnel take the following actions:

- sanitise and reset mobile devices, including all removable media
- decommission any credentials that left their possession during their travel
- report if significant doubt exists as to the integrity of any mobile devices or removable media.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > After travelling overseas with mobile devices

requirement_text:
If returning from travelling overseas with mobile devices to high or extreme risk countries, personnel take the following additional actions:

- reset credentials used with mobile devices, including those used for remote access to their organisation’s systems
- monitor user accounts for any indicators of compromise, such as failed logon attempts.
source_section: Guidelines for enterprise mobility > Mobile device usage > After travelling overseas with mobile devices

requirement_text: If procuring an evaluated product, a product that has completed a PP-based evaluation, including against all applicable PP modules (as well as a software bill of materials assessment if applicable), is selected in preference to one that has completed an EAL-based evaluation.

source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment usage > Hardening IT equipment configurations

source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment usage > Hardening IT equipment configurations

requirement_text: A networked IT equipment register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.
source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment usage > IT equipment registers

requirement_text: A non-networked IT equipment register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.
source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment usage > IT equipment registers

source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment usage > Labelling IT equipment

requirement_text: ASD’s approval is sought before applying labels to external surfaces of high assurance IT equipment.
source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment usage > Labelling high assurance IT equipment

requirement_text: IT equipment is classified based on the highest sensitivity or classification of data that it is approved for processing, storing or communicating.
source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment usage > Classifying IT equipment

requirement_text: IT equipment is handled in a manner suitable for its sensitivity or classification.
source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment usage > Handling IT equipment

source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment maintenance or repairs > Maintenance or repairs of high assurance IT equipment

source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment maintenance or repairs > On-site maintenance or repairs

requirement_text: If an appropriately cleared technician is not used to undertake maintenance or repairs to IT equipment, the IT equipment and associated media are sanitised before maintenance or repairs.
source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment maintenance or repairs > On-site maintenance or repairs

requirement_text:
If an appropriately cleared technician is not used to undertake maintenance or repairs to IT equipment, the technician is escorted by someone who:

- has the authority to direct the technician
- is appropriately cleared and briefed
- is sufficiently familiar with the IT equipment to understand the work being undertaken
- takes all responsible measures to ensure the integrity of the IT equipment
- takes due care to ensure that data is not disclosed.
source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment maintenance or repairs > On-site maintenance or repairs

source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment maintenance or repairs > Off-site maintenance or repairs

requirement_text: Following maintenance or repairs to IT equipment, it is inspected to confirm that it retains its approved configuration and that no unauthorised modifications have been made.

source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment sanitisation and destruction > IT equipment destruction processes and procedures

requirement_text: IT equipment that cannot be sanitised is destroyed.
source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment sanitisation and destruction > Sanitising IT equipment

requirement_text: IT equipment, including associated media, that is located overseas and has processed, stored or communicated AUSTEO or AGAO data, is sanitised in situ.

requirement_text: Printer and MFD platens are inspected and destroyed if any text or images are retained on the platen.
source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment sanitisation and destruction > Sanitising printers and multifunction devices

source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment sanitisation and destruction > Sanitising printers and multifunction devices

requirement_text: When unable to sanitise printer cartridges or MFD print drums, they are destroyed as per electrostatic memory devices.
source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment sanitisation and destruction > Sanitising printers and multifunction devices

source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment sanitisation and destruction > Sanitising printers and multifunction devices

requirement_text:

- following vendor sanitisation guidance
- loading a dummy configuration file, performing a factory reset and then reinstalling firmware.
source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment sanitisation and destruction > Sanitising network devices

requirement_text: IT equipment disposal processes, and supporting IT equipment disposal procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.

source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment disposal > Disposal of IT equipment

requirement_text: When disposing of IT equipment that has been designed or modified to meet emanation security standards, ASD is contacted for requirements relating to its disposal.
source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment disposal > Disposal of IT equipment

requirement_text: Following sanitisation, destruction or declassification, a formal administrative decision is made to release IT equipment, or its waste, into the public domain.
source_section: Guidelines for information technology equipment > IT equipment disposal > Disposal of IT equipment

requirement_text: A media management policy is developed, implemented and maintained.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media usage > Media management policy

requirement_text: A removable media usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media usage > Removable media usage policy

requirement_text: A removable media register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media usage > Removable media register

requirement_text: Media, except for internally mounted fixed media within information technology equipment, is labelled with protective markings reflecting its sensitivity or classification.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media usage > Labelling media

requirement_text: Media is classified to the highest sensitivity or classification of data it stores, unless the media has been classified to a higher sensitivity or classification.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media usage > Classifying media

requirement_text: Media is only used with systems that are authorised to process, store or communicate its sensitivity or classification.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media usage > Classifying media

requirement_text: Any media connected to a system with a higher sensitivity or classification than the media is reclassified to the higher sensitivity or classification, unless the media is read-only or the system has a mechanism through which read-only access can be ensured.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media usage > Reclassifying media

requirement_text: Before reclassifying media to a lower sensitivity or classification, the media is sanitised or destroyed, and a formal administrative decision is made to reclassify it.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media usage > Reclassifying media

requirement_text: All data stored on media is encrypted using ASD-approved cryptography.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media usage > Encrypting media

requirement_text: Full disk encryption, or partial encryption where access controls only allow writing to encrypted partitions or volumes, is implemented when encrypting media.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media usage > Encrypting media

requirement_text: Pre-boot authentication using passwords, or managed network-based key release, is implemented for media containing encrypted system volumes.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media usage > Encrypting media

requirement_text: Media is handled in a manner suitable for its sensitivity or classification.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media usage > Handling media

requirement_text: Media is sanitised before it is used for the first time.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media usage > Sanitising media before first use

requirement_text: Media is sanitised before it is reused in a different security domain.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media usage > Sanitising media before first use

requirement_text: When transferring data manually between two systems belonging to different security domains, write-once media is used unless the destination system has a mechanism through which read-only access can be ensured.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media usage > Using media for data transfers

requirement_text: When transferring data manually between two systems belonging to different security domains, rewritable media is sanitised after each data transfer.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media usage > Using media for data transfers

requirement_text: Media sanitisation processes, and supporting media sanitisation procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media sanitisation > Media sanitisation processes and procedures

requirement_text: Volatile media is sanitised by removing its power for at least 10 minutes.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media sanitisation > Volatile media sanitisation

requirement_text: SECRET and TOP SECRET volatile media is sanitised by overwriting it at least once in its entirety with a random pattern followed by a read back for verification.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media sanitisation > Volatile media sanitisation

requirement_text: Following sanitisation, TOP SECRET volatile media retains its classification if it stored static data for an extended period, or had data repeatedly stored on or written to the same memory location for an extended period.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media sanitisation > Treatment of volatile media following sanitisation

requirement_text: Non-volatile magnetic media is sanitised by overwriting it at least once (or three times if pre-2001 or under 15 GB) in its entirety with a random pattern followed by a read back for verification.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media sanitisation > Non-volatile magnetic media sanitisation

requirement_text: The host-protected area and device configuration overlay table are reset prior to the sanitisation of non-volatile magnetic hard drives.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media sanitisation > Non-volatile magnetic media sanitisation

requirement_text: The ATA secure erase command is used, in addition to block overwriting software, to ensure the growth defects table of non-volatile magnetic hard drives is overwritten.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media sanitisation > Non-volatile magnetic media sanitisation

requirement_text: Following sanitisation, SECRET and TOP SECRET non-volatile magnetic media retains its classification.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media sanitisation > Treatment of non-volatile magnetic media following sanitisation

requirement_text: Non-volatile EPROM media is sanitised by applying three times the manufacturer’s specified ultraviolet erasure time and then overwriting it at least once in its entirety with a random pattern followed by a read back for verification.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media sanitisation > Non-volatile erasable programmable read-only memory media sanitisation

requirement_text: Non-volatile EEPROM media is sanitised by overwriting it at least once in its entirety with a random pattern followed by a read back for verification.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media sanitisation > Non-volatile electrically erasable programmable read-only memory media sanitisation

requirement_text: Following sanitisation, SECRET and TOP SECRET non-volatile EPROM and EEPROM media retains its classification.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media sanitisation > Treatment of non-volatile erasable and electrically erasable programmable read-only memory media following sanitisation

requirement_text: Non-volatile flash memory media is sanitised by overwriting it at least twice in its entirety with a random pattern followed by a read back for verification.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media sanitisation > Non-volatile flash memory media sanitisation

requirement_text: Following sanitisation, SECRET and TOP SECRET non-volatile flash memory media retains its classification.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media sanitisation > Treatment of non-volatile flash memory media following sanitisation

requirement_text: Media that cannot be successfully sanitised is destroyed prior to its disposal.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media sanitisation > Media that cannot be successfully sanitised

requirement_text: Media destruction processes, and supporting media destruction procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Media destruction processes and procedures

requirement_text:
The following media types are destroyed prior to their disposal:

- microfiche and microfilm
- optical discs
- programmable read-only memory
- read-only memory
- other types of media that cannot be sanitised.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Media that cannot be sanitised

requirement_text: Security Construction and Equipment Committee-approved equipment or ASIO-approved equipment is used when destroying media.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Media destruction equipment

requirement_text: If using degaussers to destroy media, degaussers evaluated by the United States’ National Security Agency are used.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Media destruction equipment

requirement_text: Equipment that is capable of reducing microform to a fine powder, with resultant particles not showing more than five consecutive characters per particle upon microscopic inspection, is used to destroy microfiche and microfilm.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Media destruction methods

requirement_text: Electrostatic memory devices are destroyed using a furnace/incinerator, hammer mill, disintegrator or grinder/sander.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Media destruction methods

requirement_text: Magnetic floppy disks are destroyed using a furnace/incinerator, hammer mill, disintegrator, degausser or by cutting.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Media destruction methods

requirement_text: Magnetic hard disks are destroyed using a furnace/incinerator, hammer mill, disintegrator, grinder/sander or degausser.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Media destruction methods

requirement_text: Magnetic tapes are destroyed using a furnace/incinerator, hammer mill, disintegrator, degausser or by cutting.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Media destruction methods

requirement_text: Optical disks are destroyed using a furnace/incinerator, hammer mill, disintegrator, grinder/sander or by cutting.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Media destruction methods

requirement_text: Semiconductor memory is destroyed using a furnace/incinerator, hammer mill or disintegrator.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Media destruction methods

requirement_text: Media destroyed using a hammer mill, disintegrator, grinder/sander or by cutting results in media waste particles no larger than 9 mm.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Media destruction methods

requirement_text: The resulting media waste particles from the destruction of SECRET media is stored and handled as OFFICIAL if less than or equal to 3 mm, PROTECTED if greater than 3 mm and less than or equal to 6 mm, or SECRET if greater than 6 mm and less than or equal to 9 mm.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Treatment of media waste particles

requirement_text: The resulting media waste particles from the destruction of TOP SECRET media is stored and handled as OFFICIAL if less than or equal to 3 mm, or SECRET if greater than 3 mm and less than or equal to 9 mm.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Treatment of media waste particles

requirement_text: Magnetic media is destroyed using a degausser with a suitable magnetic field strength and magnetic orientation.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Degaussing magnetic media

requirement_text: Product-specific directions provided by degausser manufacturers are followed.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Degaussing magnetic media

requirement_text: Following the use of a degausser, magnetic media is physically damaged by deforming any internal platters.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Degaussing magnetic media

requirement_text: The destruction of media is performed under the supervision of at least one cleared person.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Supervision of destruction

requirement_text: Personnel supervising the destruction of media supervise its handling to the point of destruction and ensure that the destruction is completed successfully.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Supervision of destruction

requirement_text: The destruction of media storing accountable material is performed under the supervision of at least two cleared personnel.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Supervision of accountable material destruction

requirement_text: Personnel supervising the destruction of media storing accountable material supervise its handling to the point of destruction, ensure that the destruction is completed successfully and sign a destruction certificate afterwards.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Supervision of accountable material destruction

requirement_text: The destruction of media storing accountable material is not outsourced.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Outsourcing media destruction

requirement_text: When outsourcing the destruction of media storing non-accountable material, a National Association for Information Destruction AAA certified destruction service with endorsements, as specified in ASIO’s Protective Security Circular-167, is used.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media destruction > Outsourcing media destruction

requirement_text: Media disposal processes, and supporting media disposal procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media disposal > Media disposal processes and procedures

requirement_text: Labels and markings indicating the owner, sensitivity, classification or any other marking that can associate media with its prior use are removed prior to its disposal.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media disposal > Disposal of media

requirement_text: Following sanitisation, destruction or declassification, a formal administrative decision is made to release media, or its waste, into the public domain.
source_section: Guidelines for media > Media disposal > Disposal of media

requirement_text: Vendors that have demonstrated a commitment to Secure by Design and Secure by Default principles and practices, including secure programming practices and either memory-safe programming languages or less preferably memory-safe programming practices, are used for operating systems.

requirement_text: The latest release, or the previous release, of operating systems are used.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Operating system releases and versions

requirement_text: Where supported, 64-bit versions of operating systems are used.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Operating system releases and versions

source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Standard Operating Environments

requirement_text: SOEs provided by third parties are scanned for malicious code and configurations.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Standard Operating Environments

requirement_text: SOEs are reviewed and updated at least annually.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Standard Operating Environments

requirement_text: Approved configurations for operating systems are developed, implemented and maintained.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Hardening operating system configurations

requirement_text: Operating systems are hardened using ASD and vendor hardening guidance, with the most restrictive guidance taking precedence when conflicts occur.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Hardening operating system configurations

requirement_text: Microsoft’s attack surface reduction rules are implemented.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Hardening operating system configurations

requirement_text: Default user accounts or credentials for operating systems, including for any pre-configured user accounts, are changed, disabled or removed during initial setup.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Hardening operating system configurations

requirement_text: Unneeded user accounts, components, services and functionality of operating systems are disabled or removed.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Hardening operating system configurations

requirement_text: Automatic execution features for removable media are disabled.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Hardening operating system configurations

requirement_text: Internet Explorer 11 is disabled or removed.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Hardening operating system configurations

requirement_text: .NET Framework 3.5 (includes .NET 2.0 and 3.0) is disabled or removed.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Hardening operating system configurations

requirement_text: Operating system exploit protection functionality is enabled.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Hardening operating system configurations

requirement_text: Early Launch Antimalware, Secure Boot, Trusted Boot and Measured Boot functionality is enabled.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Hardening operating system configurations

requirement_text: Unprivileged users are prevented from bypassing, disabling or modifying security functionality of operating systems.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Hardening operating system configurations

requirement_text:
Unprivileged users are prevented from running script execution engines, including:

- Windows Script Host (cscript.exe and wscript.exe)
- PowerShell (powershell.exe, powershell_ise.exe and pwsh.exe)
- Command Prompt (cmd.exe)
- Windows Management Instrumentation (wmic.exe)
- Microsoft Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) Application Host (mshta.exe).
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Hardening operating system configurations

requirement_text: Unprivileged users do not have the ability to install unapproved applications.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Application management

requirement_text: Unprivileged users do not have the ability to uninstall or disable approved applications.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Application management

requirement_text: Application control is implemented on workstations.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Application control

requirement_text: Application control is implemented on internet-facing servers.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Application control

requirement_text: Application control is implemented on non-internet-facing servers.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Application control

requirement_text: Application control is applied to user profiles and temporary folders used by operating systems, web browsers and email clients.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Application control

requirement_text: Application control is applied to all locations other than user profiles and temporary folders used by operating systems, web browsers and email clients.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Application control

requirement_text: Application control restricts the execution of executables, libraries, scripts, installers, compiled HTML, HTML applications and control panel applets to an organisation-approved set.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Application control

requirement_text: Application control restricts the execution of drivers to an organisation-approved set.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Application control

requirement_text: Application control is implemented using cryptographic hash rules, publisher certificate rules or path rules.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Application control

requirement_text: When implementing application control using publisher certificate rules, publisher names and product names are used.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Application control

requirement_text: When implementing application control using path rules, only approved users can modify approved files and write to approved folders.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Application control

requirement_text: When implementing application control using path rules, only approved users can change file system permissions for approved files and folders.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Application control

requirement_text: Microsoft’s recommended application blocklist is implemented.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Application control

requirement_text: Microsoft’s vulnerable driver blocklist is implemented.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Application control

requirement_text: Application control rulesets are validated at least annually.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Application control

requirement_text: All users, except for local administrator accounts and break glass accounts, cannot disable, bypass or be exempted from application control.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Application control

requirement_text: Allowed and blocked application control events are centrally logged.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Application control

requirement_text: Command line process creation events are centrally logged.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Command Shell

requirement_text: Windows PowerShell 2.0 is disabled or removed.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > PowerShell

requirement_text: PowerShell is configured to use Constrained Language Mode.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > PowerShell

requirement_text: PowerShell module logging, script block logging and transcription events are centrally logged.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > PowerShell

requirement_text: PowerShell script block logs are protected by Protected Event Logging functionality.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > PowerShell

requirement_text: A HIPS or EDR solution is implemented on workstations.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Host-based intrusion detection and response solution

requirement_text: A HIPS or EDR solution is implemented on critical servers and high-value servers.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Host-based intrusion detection and response solution

requirement_text: A software firewall is implemented on workstations and servers to restrict inbound and outbound network connections to an organisation-approved set of applications and services.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Software firewall

requirement_text:
An antivirus application is implemented on workstations and servers with:

- signature-based detection functionality enabled and set to a high level
- heuristic-based detection functionality enabled and set to a high level
- reputation rating functionality enabled
- ransomware protection functionality enabled
- detection signatures configured to update at least daily
- regular scanning configured for all fixed disks and removable media.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Antivirus application

requirement_text: If there is no business requirement for reading from removable media and devices, such functionality is disabled via the use of a device access control application or by disabling external communication interfaces.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Device access control

requirement_text: If there is no business requirement for writing to removable media and devices, such functionality is disabled via the use of a device access control application or by disabling external communication interfaces.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Device access control

requirement_text: External communication interfaces that allow DMA are disabled.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Device access control

requirement_text: Security-relevant events for Apple macOS operating systems are centrally logged.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Operating system event logging

requirement_text: Security-relevant events for Linux operating systems are centrally logged.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Operating system event logging

requirement_text: Security-relevant events for Microsoft Windows operating systems are centrally logged.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Operating system hardening > Operating system event logging

requirement_text:
Services are configured with a session lock that:

- activates after a maximum of 15 minutes of user inactivity, a maximum of 12 hours of overall session time or when manually activated by users
- blocks access to all session content
- requires users to re-authenticate using all authentication factors to unlock the session
- denies users the ability to disable the session locking mechanism.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Authentication hardening > Session locking

requirement_text:
Systems are configured with a screen lock that:

- activates after a maximum of 15 minutes of user inactivity, or when manually activated by users
- conceals all content on the screen
- ensures that the screen does not enter a power saving state before the screen lock is activated
- requires users to re-authenticate using all authentication factors to unlock the system
- denies users the ability to disable the screen locking mechanism.
source_section: Guidelines for system hardening > Authentication hardening > Screen locking
